prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse 3D layout: a large oven/counter occupies the front-left foreground at roughly 0.4–1.0 m, while the standing person remains ahead near the center at about 1.3–2.0 m; rear counters, cabinets, and the bright window lie farther away, roughly 2–4 m. The person stands behind and slightly right of the oven, with the sink/counter beside them, while the floor extends between the camera wearer and those surfaces; nearby foreground edges are clearer here than in the bright, distorted RGB view. Across the five frames, the oven and counter shift toward the left as the camera turns right, while the person moves from center-left to center-right in the image without a clear large change in distance; in the last frame, the camera wearer’s raised hands enter very near the camera, within about 0.2–0.5 m. Depth around the window, the person’s outline, thin objects, and frame boundaries is unreliable, with abrupt dark or bright regions and inconsistent object boundaries that prevent precise metre estimates or dependable person-facing direction.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates the standing person from the kitchen fixtures and identifies an oven, sink, refrigerator, bottles or cups, books, and a potted plant; spatially, the oven is front-left, the sink is behind or to the right of it, the refrigerator is beside the standing person, and the small items sit above them on counters or shelves. Using the RGB context, the oven is approximately 0.5–1.2 m from the camera wearer, the standing person and nearby refrigerator are about 1.3–2.0 m away and within roughly 0.3–0.8 m of each other, while the labelled small objects are generally beyond the camera wearer’s arm reach but within the standing person’s reach. Across the frames, the person remains upright ahead while shifting from left-of-center to right-of-center as the viewpoint turns; the oven mask becomes prominent in frames 3–5, and the final frame contains a partly visible foreground person-shaped mask at the far right corresponding to extremely close, partly cropped foreground body or hands. The map makes object extents and occlusion relationships easier to see than RGB alone, but labels such as “toilet,” “book,” and some small-object fragments appear unreliable, several fixtures change colour or extent between frames, and black unlabeled areas hide much of the room.
descriptions.pose: The pose map shows one standing person about 1.3–2.0 m in front of the camera wearer, generally upright and facing approximately toward the camera, with the head and shoulders oriented frontally or slightly turned rather than showing a clear back view. Their arms are raised near head or chest height across the sequence, with hands above the torso and therefore within their own arm’s reach; the magenta hand cluster is detected clearly only in the first frame, while no reliable camera-wearer skeleton is shown. The skeleton shifts from left-of-center to right-of-center as the camera viewpoint turns, and its changing shoulder, elbow, and head geometry suggests modest body or upper-body turning, but no strong approach or retreat is evident. Pose makes limb arrangement, joint height, and facing direction clearer than RGB alone, yet several wrists, hands, facial points, feet, and isolated dots are missing or misplaced, so exact gaze direction, hand distance, occlusion by the body, and metre-scale separation cannot be recovered reliably from this map.
